news.title: Falling wages, soaring energy prices and inflation: It’s beginning to look a lot like the 1970s
news.description: Is it time to dust off the financial playbook from that dismal decade?
news.author: Brett Arends

copy.hook: Your pay rose 5%. So why could you buy less?
copy.explain: In 1973 oil jumped from $3 to $12 a barrel, lifting prices on almost everything. Prices rose about 10% a year, so a 5% raise bought less: real pay, what money buys, shrank.
copy.takeaway: Judge any gain by what it buys, not by the number.
copy.question: If oil spiked like it did in 1973, which of your bills would hurt first?
